newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH CBANK SAYS LEAVES MONETARY POLICY UNCHANGED.
newsitem.headline: CZECH CBANK SAYS LEAVES MONETARY POLICY UNCHANGED.

text.p: The Czech National Bank (CNB) said on Thursday that it had left monetary policy unchanged at its regular board meeting on Thursday afternoon.
In a statement the CNB said that its monetary policy was appropriate to current circumstances.

"The governing board of the Czech National Bank at its meeting today considered the current data on economic and monetary developments. It decided that (the current) monetary policy is appropriate to the current situation and there is no need to change it," the statement said.
Dealers had been closely watching for the outcome of the CNB board meeting fearing that the central bank may heed government calls for a relaxation of monetary policy and cut interest rates.

Last summer the CNB raised the discount rate to 10.5 percent from 9.5 percent and the lombard rate to 14 percent from 12.5 percent. It also raised minimum reserve requirements to 11.5 percent from 8.5 percent but two weeks ago cut reserve requirements back to 9.5 percent.
